grh_8a2c41551928f9b81189.title: Mother in law Story
paragraphs: Wilma Parker and Howard Ross have repeatedly tried to marry, but Howard's devotion to his widowed mother keeps interfering. He has already sacrificed a promising job rather than leave Mrs. Ross, and another illness on their wedding day postpones the ceremony for a third time. The town begins to believe Mrs. Ross is deliberately preventing the marriage, and she finally admits to Dr. Christian that she does not want Howard to marry because she fears losing the son around whom she has built her life. Wilma feels humiliated and rejected, while Howard becomes too proud and angry to repair the break. During a heavy snowstorm Howard is working on a utility line when he slips and is seriously injured. With telephone lines down and Howard missing for hours, Wilma and Mrs. Ross are left together for seven agonizing hours, each fearing that the man they both love may die. Their rivalry gives way to honesty: Mrs. Ross admits she was wrong to treat Wilma as someone taking Howard away, and both realize there was room in his life for them both. Howard survives, and after the crisis the wedding finally takes place. Christian later observes that giving the two women time alone to talk accomplished what argument could not.

paragraphs: A dramatization of Egon Hostovsky's The Hideout follows a Czech engineer living secretly in a cellar after fleeing Nazi persecution and becoming cut off from his wife and former life. His long isolation turns inward until a chance encounter with an old German acquaintance and contact with resistance members force him to confront the selfishness and fear behind his hiding.
